title: Keyturn Host Protection Plan: Raising the Host's Own Share of an Accepted Loss
content:
Every accepted loss carries the host's own share, booked against the enrolment the claim was made under. The host's share of a loss is fixed only after an appraisal of that loss stands on the enrolment with the money it accepts booked as owed to the host. The share is raised on the Keyturn Host Protection Plan enrolment the claim belongs to and is shown against that claim.

### Situation of use and capability

`raise_host_share_c19fa66d` writes a host-share record against the named claim and increases the amount the host owes on the enrolment by that figure. The host can afterwards see the charge against the claim and the higher amount owed by them on the enrolment.

### How it is invoked

The tool is unlocked and then called by the desk agent, who works the share out and passes it in.

### Parameters

- `enrollment_id` — the reference number of the host protection enrolment the share is raised on, read from the enrolment record retrieved for this host.
- `source_claim_id` — the reference number of the accepted claim record the share belongs to, read from the claim records standing on that enrolment.
- `booking_id` — the reference number of the trip booking the loss happened on, read from the claim record the share belongs to.
- `damage_category` — the kind of loss the share belongs to, one of `exterior_body`, `interior`, `glass`, `tyres_wheels`, `mechanical`, `theft_total_loss`, `missing_equipment` and `third_party_property`.
- `liability_finding` — who the marketplace found responsible for the loss, one of `undetermined`, `guest_at_fault`, `host_at_fault`, `third_party` and `no_fault`.
- `host_share_amount` — the amount the host carries on this loss, in USD, 2 decimal places, signed, passed as a positive figure rounded half-up to the cent.

### Return

A confirmation line in plain text carrying the reference number of the host-share record, the claim it belongs to, the amount raised in USD to the cent and the enrolment's new amount owed by the host. Receiving that line means the share now stands against the host; no other output is produced.
